title: VPC Peering & Private Endpoints 🔗
description: Connect VPCs together and access AWS services without internet exposure.

slides.title: VPC Peering ↔️
slides.content:
# Direct VPC‑to‑VPC Connection

**VPC Peering** connects two VPCs privately using the AWS backbone. Instances in different VPCs can communicate as if they’re in the same network.

- Can be within the same region or **cross‑region**.
- Can be between different AWS accounts.
- Peering is not transitive: if VPC A peers with B and B peers with C, A cannot talk to C through B.
- No overlapping CIDR blocks allowed.

**Use cases**: Shared services VPC (logging, authentication) connecting to application VPCs.

quizData.question: VPC A is peered with VPC B. VPC B is peered with VPC C. Can an instance in A talk to an instance in C?

options.text: Only if both are in the same region

quizData.explanation: VPC Peering is a one‑to‑one relationship. For hub‑and‑spoke, use AWS Transit Gateway.

slides.title: VPC Endpoints: Private Access to AWS Services 🛡️
slides.content:
# No Internet Needed

Many AWS services (S3, DynamoDB, SNS, etc.) are public by default – they live on the internet. To access them privately from your VPC, use a **VPC Endpoint**.

Two types:
- **Gateway Endpoint**: S3 and DynamoDB only. Adds a route to your route table; traffic goes through the endpoint.
- **Interface Endpoint**: All other services (via AWS PrivateLink). Creates an Elastic Network Interface (ENI) in your subnet with a private IP.

Traffic never leaves the AWS network, improving security and reducing data transfer costs.

slides.title: Gateway vs Interface Endpoint 🆚
slides.content:
# Which One?

- **Gateway Endpoint**: Free. Supports S3 and DynamoDB. Configured via route table entry.
- **Interface Endpoint**: Hourly cost + data processing fee. Supports most AWS services (KMS, SSM, SQS, etc.). Uses DNS to resolve to private IP.

**Example**: An EC2 instance in a private subnet can download patches from S3 via a Gateway Endpoint, without a NAT Gateway.

quizData.question: Which VPC endpoint type is required for accessing AWS Systems Manager (SSM) privately?

options.text: SSM does not support VPC endpoints

quizData.explanation: SSM uses an Interface Endpoint (PrivateLink). Only S3 and DynamoDB support Gateway Endpoints.

slides.title: AWS PrivateLink 🔗
slides.content:
# Share Your Own Services Privately

**AWS PrivateLink** lets you expose a service (e.g., your own application) as an endpoint in another VPC or to other AWS accounts.

- You create a **Network Load Balancer** in your VPC, then a PrivateLink endpoint service.
- Consumers create an Interface Endpoint to connect.
- Traffic stays within AWS, avoiding the internet.

This is how SaaS providers on AWS deliver services to their customers securely.
